proposed_fixes.title: FancyZones window restore can change Chrome size across mixed-DPI monitors
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Restore placement may recompute a window rectangle using stale monitor/DPI work-area dimensions after minimize/restore on a different-DPI display.
plan: Trace FancyZones placement before minimize and after restore on the mixed-DPI laptop/external display.
Use the restored window's current monitor DPI/work area when reapplying zone bounds.
Add a regression test for restore across mixed-DPI monitor topology.
verification: Minimize/restore Chrome on the external display and verify its bounds stay within the same zone under mixed scaling.

confidence.rationale: A stale DPI/monitor rectangle is plausible, but the report predates current FancyZones and may have changed.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming this on the original laptop and supplying a bugreport. Your workaround changed the laptop resolution or closed its lid, which points toward mixed-DPI placement. Could you confirm the current PowerToys version and whether Chrome still crosses the zone on the latest release? If so, please give the current resolution/scaling of the laptop and external displays. This determines whether the original DPI topology is still reproducible.
